newsitem.title: USA: Exide to close four European battery plants.
newsitem.headline: Exide to close four European battery plants.

text.p: Exide Corp said it plans to close four battery making plants in Europe in the coming year while the financial health of the company looks set to improve futher.
"Our outlook for financial performance for fiscal 1998 is truly outstanding," Chairman Arthur Hawkins told an analyst conference call on Wednesday, later made available on tape.

Profits in North America will be boosted following a decision by Sears, Roebuck & Co. to expand Exide's role as a supplier of batteries to the company, thereby increasing its North American market share, Hawkins said.
The company's new NASCAR battery and battery accessories will also generate extra profits, Hawkins added.
Exide is the world's biggest producer of batteries and a key player in the lead market.

Exide on Tuesday announced a loss of $10.6 million, or 50 cents per share, for its fourth quarter, including a one-time loss to retire debt early. It earned $16.2 million, or 77 cents, for fiscal 1997.
A mild winter in North America forced Exide to cut battery production by a million units in the fourth quarter.
Restructuring and closing some European plants in fiscal 1997 along with non-recurring changes in balance sheet reporting also dented results. Some 1,000 staff at Exide were laid off in fiscal 1997.
Four battery making plants in Europe will be closed in fiscal 1998, Dagenham in Britain, Nimes and Vierzon in France, and Horten in Norway, saving $24 million, Hawkins said.
And a further two plants will close in Germany following the takeover of CEAG AG, with the loss of some 500 jobs, he said. The takeover is set to be completed next month.
Exide stock fell 50 cents to $20.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
